study.question: Does the fraction of nonmatching field/action events occurring after the newest same-field target match recover conditional temporal-order information that the incumbent mean/max decay summaries omit, and does correct field anchoring matter?
study.hypothesis: Observed: r0011-nonmatch_latest AUC 0.6193279424 exceeds nonmatch_mean 0.6187407113 by 0.0005872312, but activity_latest already reaches 0.6192250013 (binding gap only 0.0001029411). The candidate diagnostics on the first 512 report mean latest-binding distance only 0.0043507074; these source-scrutinized measurements are descriptive. The incumbent compresses event ages into sums, one-day extrema and log2 buckets, so histories with identical inherited summaries can differ in how much activity follows the latest target match. Provisional mechanism: explicitly supplying this empirical relative order helps distinguish persistent from interrupted target-related activity; nonmatching events are never negative preference labels. A positive result requires rank to beat the smooth proxy AND correctly anchored rank to beat swapped-field rank, beyond seed uncertainty. Ordering is chronological association, not a causal transition.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the local target-aware activation idea through the task adaptation. DIN explicitly abandons softmax normalization at lines 270-277; this ancestor retains normalized pooling. The proposed branch computes an empirical comparison of supplied event ages around a newest-match anchor rather than a learned activation pool. It is not an exact DIN reproduction, and priority for conditional rank features is unverified.

README confirms category, brand, behavior-type histories without item identities. This model uses exactly those supplied fields and ages. Publisher paper detail remains unavailable, so no detailed DMR mechanism or priority comparison is claimed.

Retain its full 40 scalar coordinates, static features and retrieval. Add eight order fractions. Unlike a raw newest-event maximum, each fraction compares every nonmatching event to the newest matching event within action, and is invariant to strictly monotone age transformations before float quantization. Swapped anchors and smooth marginal-decay proxies separate field binding and information beyond decay moments.

study.proposed_difference: For each category/brand and action, find newest matching age a_f and collect nonmatching ages t. Rank coordinate R_f=mean(1[t<a_f]+0.5*1[t=a_f]). Swap a_category and a_brand in the crossed control. Smooth proxy P_f=0.5+0.5*(mean(exp(-ln(2)*t/86400))-exp(-ln(2)*a_f/86400)); it uses marginal mean decay and anchor maximum without empirical order counts. All four cells zero all coordinates for an action unless both fields have known targets, at least one target match and at least one nonmatch. This support gate is identical across cells. Append eight coordinates with 1024 zero weights after constructing the exact complete parent. No optimizer/loss, input, history selection or data changes. All four summaries computed in every variant. This is a bounded deterministic event-order representation; broad architectural novelty remains unverified.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrasts: AUC(aligned_rank)-AUC(aligned_decay)>0 and AUC(aligned_rank)-AUC(crossed_rank)>0; report both separately and the factorial interaction (aligned_rank-aligned_decay)-(crossed_rank-crossed_decay). Candidate should also improve on r0011-nonmatch_latest, otherwise no practical gain is supported. Differences remain preliminary until paired seeds.

Exact constructed histories can hold all explicit parent counts/masses/extrema and recency embedding buckets fixed while order fraction changes; inherited retrieval then also sees identical event embeddings. This is a representational witness, not measured predictive value. Concrete analytic witness: one matching event with decay 0.5 and four nonmatches with decays [0.9,0.55,0.2,0.1] versus [0.9,0.45,0.3,0.1], all same action and both fields sharing the match partition. Counts, decay sums, matching/nonmatching maxima, means and pair-support statistics agree; corresponding event recency buckets [17,14,17,18,19] agree; the order fraction is 0.50 versus 0.25 and smooth proxy is 0.46875 in both. Under standard-library float32-age approximation, maximum inherited-summary difference was 3.717444130302283e-09. This is analytic/scalar evidence of a representation limitation, not actual Torch bitwise equivalence or predictive mechanism support.

New features lie in [0,1] and vanish for unsupported, unknown-target and empty-history cases. Full-history duplication and permutation preserve fractions; ties receive 0.5. Rank coordinates stay invariant under common strictly increasing transforms of nonnegative ages, when ordering/ties survive floating quantization.

The common support gate may sharply reduce usable brand/action cases. Report per-action support in the authorized diagnostic sample and mark population slice inference unavailable. Equal anchors make binding controls identical by construction; report supported equal-anchor fraction. No changes to predictions for empty histories arise from the new coordinates at a fixed checkpoint.
falsifiers: If aligned_rank does not beat aligned_decay, empirical ordering beyond smooth marginal moments is unsupported in this implementation. If rank improves but crossed rank is equal or better, correct field anchoring is unsupported.

If both proxy and rank improve similarly over parent, extra basis/gating or capacity remains sufficient; do not attribute gain to conditional temporal order. If all cells lose, retain incumbent and record all null/negative outcomes.

If support is absent/very sparse or crossed/align features are nearly identical, this design lacks a discriminating test on available data; diagnose support/correlation before asserting a mechanism failure.

If inequalities, absence gates, empty-history finiteness, source boundaries or host execution fail, the implementation is invalid and consumed costs remain charged. An execution failure is not scientific counterevidence.

Common support gate reveals conjunctions of field/action presence and may explain apparent gains
Swapped-field anchors share many same events; correlated category and brand can weaken the binding control
Age ordering may reflect activity density, history truncation or unverified static-snapshot timing rather than preference evolution
Inherited count statistics and attention can carry generic activity intensity; the parent is a task adaptation, not a faithful original DIN replication
